history.summary: DUPLICATE FLAG: this row is the SAME temple as seq 2066 'Kodamdeshwar Temple' (which was already flagged as a duplicate of seq 864 'Kodamdesar Bhairav Temple') - recommend merging the CSV rows. CSV TOWN FLAG: the historic temple is at Kodamdesar village, ~24-30 km west of Bikaner city on the Bikaner-Jaisalmer highway, opposite Gajner Palace - NOT in Bikaner city; documented with the corrected town. COORDINATE FLAG: the geocoder has no listing for Kodamdesar village, so the coordinates here mirror seq 2066's file (an in-city listing also called 'Kodamdesar Bhairav Temple' in Lalgarh) and are approximate for the village site. Rao Bika, founder of Bikaner, first chose Kodamdesar for his capital and installed the Bhairuji idol here (local lore says on Karni Mata's orders; a legend links the place to Kodamde, Vikram Samvat 1465 - verify) before shifting to the present Bikaner site. The temple is famously open-air: legend holds that no roof can ever be built over the idol; the floor is white marble and a pond lies behind the temple. It is popular with newly married couples seeking blessings and for mundan (first hair-shaving) ceremonies; two sati cenotaphs stand nearby.

name: Kodamdesar Temple
town: Kodamdesar (CSV town 'Bikaner' is imprecise - the temple is at Kodamdesar village, ~24-30 km west on the Jaisalmer highway)
town_description: Kodamdesar is a small desert village on the Bikaner-Jaisalmer highway opposite Gajner Palace, ~24-30 km west of Bikaner, with the Kodamdesar Lake/pond behind the temple - a quiet pilgrimage stop amid Thar scrub.

travel.airport: Bikaner (Nal) Airport; the temple is a ~40-minute taxi/private-car ride from Bikaner on the Jaisalmer highway (verify distance from airport).
travel.railway: Bikaner Junction - about 26-29 km; buses and private taxis ply the Jaisalmer road.
travel.road: On the Bikaner-Jaisalmer highway, opposite Gajner Palace; the temple entry gate is easily visible from the highway.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; the Bhadrapad fair (August-September) is the biggest occasion.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Generally open during daylight hours (no published timings - verify on site). Dress modestly and remove footwear; photography is allowed per visitor reports; prasad is available outside the premises.
